- [LGRA.2.9.6.11] **A spec on a `Json` leaf is checked when the leaf is read.**
  The compiler cannot know a `Json` leaf's kind, so [LGRA.2.9.6.5]'s refusals
  bind only a value whose kind is known statically, and the compiler must
  accept a spec on a leaf. At run time, a spec part that the leaf's kind does
  not take under [LGRA.2.9.6.5]'s rules is a **TypeError**, as any operation
  on a wrong-typed leaf is ([LEXP.7.12.1]): the activation is abandoned and
  the fault reaches the fault surfaces ([LERR.9.1]). The runtime must not render the
  value with the spec part dropped. A leaf whose kind takes the spec renders
  as [LGRA.2.9.6.10] states.

  Only a leaf renders. A path that reaches an object or an array is not a
  leaf, and interpolating it is a TypeError, with or without a spec, with the
  same disposition as above.

  A whole `Json` value ([LEXP.7.19]) is not a leaf, whatever it holds. The
  compiler must refuse interpolating one, or a `let` bound to one
  ([LGRA.2.9.6.2]), with `DS_VALIDATE_INTERP_UNSUPPORTED` ([LGRA.2.9.6.9]), with
  or without a spec.
